Hi Alice & Brian,

Thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

What I heard on the call:
- Workload: inference for clinical triage models, contains PHI/PII.
- Data residency: must stay in us-east-1; no cross-region egress unless explicitly approved.
- Retention: patient data retained up to 7 years for compliance.
- Logging/audit: need full request/response audit logs, but with token redaction for PII.
- Deployment preference: Private VPC or on-prem/air-gapped if required for additional controls.

Open questions we called out (please confirm):
1) Can you confirm the classification for inputs (PII only vs PHI + PII)?
2) Is any downstream egress allowed (S3 uploads, analytics pipelines) or must we guarantee no egress from the VPC?
3) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM?
4) Any procurement/PS timelines we should be aware of?

Attachments: I uploaded a first-pass dataflow diagram for discussion (acme-vpc-dataflow-diagram.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Technical review: Neha to provide a short architecture note covering VPC peering, egress controls, and options for on-prem air-gap. (target 2 business days)
- Share SOC2 type II evidence and KMS options.
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with your security and platform teams next week.

Would Wednesday (11/03) or Thursday (11/04) work for a deep-dive?

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Classification: inputs will include PHI (patient identifiers, medical notes) and PII (name, email). We treat both as sensitive; PHI controls are required.
- Retention: we need the ability to set retention policies up to 7 years; some records will be shorter (30-90 days) but ability to configure per-dataset is required.
- Egress: short answer is we need to avoid external egress. Any model hosting must not send data outside our VPC boundaries. Exceptions require written approval from our security team.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (we use AWS KMS currently) for at-rest encryption of model artifacts and logs.

Can you confirm if Redwood supports: 1) private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering, 2) audit logs with PII redaction, and 3) a path to an air-gapped on-prem deployment if needed?

Also please share SOC2 Type II evidence and any platform architecture docs. Brian will coordinate procurement timing.

On the deep-dive: Thursday 11/04 morning PT works for our security engineers.

Best,
Alice

Hi Alice — thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical note in response to your items and the questions from Marissa: 

1) Deployment options:
   - Private VPC (recommended): Redwood can run a private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering. In this mode, inference workers are deployed into a dedicated subnet in your VPC (no public IPs) and all egress can be blocked by security groups + policy.
   - Private with Redwood-managed control plane: we can offer a private control plane that communicates to your VPC via private endpoints. This is simpler operationally but requires a small set of outbound connections for control traffic — we can describe and allowlist endpoints.
   - On-prem / air-gapped: supported via our Private (on-prem) package. This requires an on-site deployment and offline build artifacts; connectivity is fully gated (no outbound telemetry unless you enable it). Longer lead time and engagement with our infra org.

2) KMS/HSM:
   - We support customer-managed KMS in AWS (bring-your-own-key) and can integrate with customer HSMs for key wrapping.

3) Audit logs & redaction:
   - We provide request-level audit logs and can enable token redaction. We also offer configurable retention windows for logs and model inputs.

4) Data residency & egress controls:
   - For private VPC deployments we can guarantee that inference traffic and logs remain in the configured region. Additional controls (NACLs, security groups, route table configurations) can be pre-configured as part of the deployment runbook.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf (high-level architecture + required network allowlist), SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2025.pdf (share link included in my next email).

Next actionable items from engineering:
- I will draft a deployment runbook for the private VPC option outlining required network configs and egress blocking steps (EOD 10/30).
- If AcmeHealth needs air-gapped on-prem, we will need a scoping call to discuss hardware and build pipeline constraints.

Cc'ing Marissa to coordinate scheduling.
